payload.title: Wedding Planning Checklist Month by Month, From 12 Months Out
protect_keywords: wedding planning checklist month by month
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, newly engaged or a few months in, with a generous budget and a destination wedding on the table, who want one month-by-month list that tells them what to do now, what can wait, and what changes when the wedding is overseas (passports, legal paperwork for marrying abroad, guest travel and room blocks, insurance timing), so nothing that has a fixed lead time is left too late.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination wedding (single primary CTA, placed after the 8 to 9 months section where venue, vendors and guest travel converge); /magazine as a soft secondary link in the close.
payload.angle: Most month-by-month checklists are written for a local wedding and treat a destination wedding as a footnote. This one runs two tracks side by side: the core planning tasks for each month from 12 months out to the week of, and a destination track beside each month for the things with fixed lead times that a local checklist misses (passport validity and renewal, legal documents for marrying overseas or marrying legally at home first, guest room blocks and travel, and when to take out travel insurance). Every legal and travel timing comes from an official source, every task is written as practical advice rather than statistics, and the whole plan closes with a printable recap table.
must_include: Intro (short, no year), then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
Prominent early link to the pillar /expert-advice/wedding-planning-checklist (as the full checklist hub) and a link to /meh-to-magnificent-wedding-planning-timeline (timeline)

Ten month-by-month sections in order: 12 months out; 10 to 11 months out; 8 to 9 months out; 6 to 7 months out; 4 to 5 months out; 3 months out; 2 months out; 1 month out; The final 2 weeks; The week of the wedding. Each is a short checklist of practical tasks drawn from: budget, guest list, venue, planner or Wedded Advisor, vendors, attire, invitations, rings, legal paperwork, guest travel, final confirmations; written as advice, never statistics

A 'Destination track' beside each month: passports (validity and renewal timing from the official Australian Passport Office), guest travel and room blocks, legal documents for marrying overseas (CNI per DFAT/smartraveller, or marrying legally in Australia first), and travel insurance timing (from smartraveller guidance: take it out when you book)

Australian legal paperwork only as officially stated: NOIM lodged with the celebrant no earlier than 18 months and no later than one month before the wedding (Attorney-General's Department) [[VERIFY]]; link /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage and /expert-advice/name-change-after-marriage (both draft) where relevant
Link /expert-advice/destination-wedding-checklist from the destination track and /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline from the week-of section
Printable recap table: rows = the ten time blocks; columns = core tasks and destination track (short phrases)
FAQ (4 to 6 questions, no prices, no averages, no legal advice beyond official facts)
Close linking /wonderland-concierge (primary, Advisor claims from brand-facts.md only) and /magazine
avoid: Prices, amounts, deposits or budget percentages
Vendor, venue or brand names (other than Wedded Wonderland brand terms); no photo credits copied from the old page
'Best' anywhere, including the old comparison table's 'Best for' row
'Most couples', averages, typical booking lead times or any statistic (old page used 'Most couples plan for 12 to 18 months')
Fixed invitation or RSVP week counts presented as rules unless sourced; frame as advice

Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md (single point of contact; works in the couple's time zone; fee and inclusions agreed in writing; room blocks with Wedded Privileges; plans venue, travel, vendors and payments). Never say the Advisor handles legal paperwork, NOIM, CNI or visas
'Marriage licence' framing (US); in Australia it is the NOIM and celebrant
Wonderland Studio feature claims (template task counts, 7-day free trial, 'eleven tools', reminders) unless confirmed; brand-facts lists Studio only as a planning app (seating chart, RSVP)
Reusing old-page or competitor wording; any reference to an 'old version' of the page
Research talk in the copy (sources, what could or couldn't be found, method)
Year in the title or dated framing (2024)
